concerns.location: plan.md: Project Structure, src/interpret/attention_attribution.py; spec FR-003/FR-008
concerns.text: The model is a plain 2-layer Bi-LSTM (FR-003) with no attention layer, yet the plan implements `attention_attribution.py` to satisfy FR-008 ('attention weight analysis'). A standard stacked Bi-LSTM has no attention weights to extract; attention-based attribution is undefined for this architecture. Either the model must include an attention mechanism (changing FR-003's architecture) or FR-008 must be re-scoped (e.g., gradient×input or integrated gradients as the third attribution method). As planned, this analysis cannot produce a valid result.

concerns.location: plan.md: Task Mapping SC-009/SC-010; spec SC-009/SC-010
concerns.text: Feature-space mismatch between the model's importance outputs and the validation criteria. SHAP/permutation on the Bi-LSTM rank raw time-step×channel inputs (15,000 features), but SC-010 validates 'top-5 features' against literature signatures like 'variance of the ΔQ(V) curve' and 'incremental-capacity peak shifts' — derived features that are not in the model's input space. Likewise SC-009's linear regression on 'top-5 features' is ill-specified: regressing on 5 individual time-step values will almost certainly fail R² ≥ 0.30 and p < 0.05 regardless of model quality. The plan needs an explicit mapping/aggregation step (e.g., aggregate time-step importances into channel/cycle-window or derived-signature features) or the criteria need re-scoping.

Target heterogeneity: fade is 'measured at the end of cycle 100 (or the last available cycle if fewer than 100)'. Cells cycled to different depths before EOL have targets defined at different cycle counts, conflating early-life fade with long-term degradation and adding target noise that biases R² and the SC-007 ΔR² comparison. The plan should either restrict to cells with ≥100 cycles (and state the expected cell-count cost against FR-011's ≥30-cell requirement) or justify/stratify by target horizon.

The plan itself concedes power for ΔR² = 0.05 at tens-of-cells N will 'likely show power < 0.8'. Since SC-007's ≥0.05 threshold is then uninterpretable as a pass/fail criterion, the plan should state upfront how SC-007 will be adjudicated (e.g., report ΔR² with CI and treat the threshold as descriptive) rather than deferring the contradiction to the results phase.

FR-001 mandates Battery Archive ('No other dataset source may be substituted') but no verified programmatic download endpoint exists; the plan correctly blocks all result-producing tasks (SC-001, SC-002, SC-004–SC-007, SC-009, SC-010 unmeasurable). The spec itself is the root cause: it must either name a verified open mirror/endpoint for Battery Archive (or an equivalent multi-protocol battery cycling dataset) or relax FR-001 to permit a verified substitute. Until then FR-001, FR-011, FR-012 and eight SCs are unbacked in practice — route to clarified.

Confirmed from the data-resources lens: the plan's core data resource is unobtainable as specified. FR-001 mandates Battery Archive with 'No other dataset source may be substituted', yet no verified programmatic endpoint exists, and none of the verified URLs (crop/sea-ice/audio/3D-model) contain voltage/current/temperature cycling traces or capacity-fade targets — they are wrong-domain datasets and cannot serve even as partial substitutes. The plan correctly refuses synthetic stand-ins (FR-012), so no result-producing task (SC-001/004/005/006/007/009/010) can run. The scope-revision request (verified mirror/endpoint, e.g. a Zenodo/HF snapshot of Battery Archive or Severson et al. 2019 data, OR relaxing FR-001) must be resolved at the spec level before this plan can be approved as executable; the plan should not advance to tasks with all result paths blocked.

SC-009 runs linear regression with p-values on the top-5 features that were SELECTED by importance analysis on the same trained model/data. Selecting features and then testing their significance on the same sample is circular (selection-then-inference); the p<0.05 and R²≥0.30 criteria are biased toward rejection of the null by construction. The plan must evaluate the top-5 regression on data disjoint from the selection set (e.g., select on training cells, fit/test the regression on held-out cells), or use a post-selection inference correction.

The baseline feature 'dq_variance_10_100' (Severson-style ΔQ(V) variance over cycles 10–100) uses cycles beyond the model's 50-cycle predictor window. This creates an information asymmetry: either the baseline is given MORE information than the Bi-LSTM (making SC-007's ΔR²≥0.05 comparison confounded) or it violates the FR-010 early-cycle-only principle. The plan must state which cycle window the baseline features use and align it with the 50-cycle window.

MC-dropout with 10 forward passes produces uncalibrated intervals; there is no guarantee (or mechanism in the plan) that coverage reaches the SC-006 target of ≥0.90. The plan should either add a calibration step (e.g., conformalized residuals on a validation split) or reframe SC-006 as reporting achieved coverage rather than a pass/fail target the method cannot control.

concerns.location: spec.md Assumptions (fade definition); data-model.md SequenceWindow target_fade
concerns.text: The target is fade at cycle 100 'or the last available cycle if fewer than 100'. Cells censored at different cycle counts have mechanically smaller fade (less time to degrade), so target values are confounded with cell lifetime/protocol. This is especially damaging for the unseen-protocol holdout (SC-004): apparent protocol generalization failure/success may reflect differing censoring points across protocol families. The plan should restrict to cells with ≥100 cycles or model censoring explicitly.

SC-010 requires ≥3 of the top-5 ranked features to 'correspond to' literature signatures (ΔQ(V) variance, fade slope, IC peak shifts), but the model's ranked features are raw time-step/channel positions (e.g., voltage at cycle 30, step 45), not derived electrochemical quantities. The plan never defines the mapping from a time-step feature to a derived signature, making the validation unfalsifiable as specified. Define the correspondence rule (e.g., aggregate time-step importances into channel/cycle-window summaries comparable to the literature features) before this criterion can be assessed.
